crossRefs.note: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.
The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.
My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my plague. My kinsmen stand far away.
You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to them. I am confined, and I can’t escape.
You have put lover and friend far from me, and my friends into darkness.
Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not…
But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you, and personally drag you before the courts?
Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but shall not be heard.
He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.
And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,
and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs…
But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how…
My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

translations.web: All the relatives of the poor shun him: how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.
translations.bsb: All the brothers of a poor man hate him— how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
translations.kjv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words,
translations.asv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth them with words, but they are gone.
